- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates or overreacts to sharp drops; increase early forecast lows and avoid extreme negative spikes.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 2024-09-23, 2025-04-17) — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior 18-day average.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast shows strong upward trend from 18-day history, reduce later forecast values; if downward, avoid premature bottoming.
- Sentiment + history correlation: if sentiment is positive but price history shows consolidation, model overreacts — dampen forecast volatility.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overestimate early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive; adjust downward by 10–20% for first 5 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust — force a downward correction in forecast from day 8 onward, especially if true outcome shows sharp drop.
